Staff Regulatory Affairs Specialist

About the Role

The Staff Regulatory Affairs Specialist plays a key role in advancing the regulatory success of Natera in the fields of women's health, oncology, and organ transplantation worldwide. Working within a team of regulatory professionals and alongside project teams, you will prepare the regulatory submissions required to market new or modified in vitro diagnostic devices in domestic and international clinical markets, and contribute to the development and implementation of regulatory strategies across Natera's products and services.

You will bring established technical knowledge and an understanding of regulatory requirements in at least one area of regional expertise (e.g., US FDA, CAP/CLIA/NYS, EU, Japan, or China), and you will grow into additional areas to support the approval, registration, and licensure of Natera's products and services. You will plan, coordinate, and report on regulatory projects of low to moderate complexity, recommend appropriate actions on regulatory issues, and escalate more complex matters to RA leadership.

You will serve as a core team member for assigned projects and product lines, collaborating with project teams to ensure the product development process, including clinical studies, addresses regulatory requirements and business objectives. You will also represent the RA team to internal and external stakeholders, provide regulatory analysis and impact assessments on legislation and industry guidance, and maintain product registrations, change assessments, post-market surveillance reports, laboratory licenses, and records of communication with regulatory authorities.

What You'll Do (under limited supervision)

Regulatory Submissions and Authority Interactions

  • Prepare and coordinate regulatory submissions for new and modified in vitro diagnostic devices, including IDEs, EU/IVD Technical Documentation, classification requests, pre-submissions, and registrations worldwide, with guidance from RA leadership on more complex filings
  • Prepare analytical and clinical pre-submissions to regulatory authorities in partnership with RA leadership
  • Author low to moderate complexity marketing and investigational use applications, and support high complexity applications for new or modified products
  • Conduct written communication with regulatory authorities on behalf of Regulatory Affairs, and support meetings with authorities through preparation, participation, and follow-up
  • Maintain accurate records of regulatory interactions and reports

Regulatory Strategy and Compliance

  • Develop and help execute regulatory strategies for low to moderate complexity programs, escalating complex or novel issues to RA leadership
  • Interpret and communicate regulatory requirements within a particular area of IVDs (CLIA/CAP/NYS, US FDA, or EU IVDR), and build working knowledge of additional areas
  • Prepare regulatory plans and change assessments that meet CAP/CLIA/NYS, US IVD, EU IVDR, and international requirements
  • Advocate least-burdensome approaches that facilitate time-to-market for Natera products and services
  • Review regulatory compliance of advertising, promotion, and labeling across a product line
  • Support implementation and maintenance of regulatory department procedures, including gap assessments for new or modified standards and regulations
  • Support quality and regulatory audits and inspections

Cross-Functional Project Leadership

  • Represent Regulatory Affairs on designated project teams and serve as the regulatory contact for assigned products or projects
  • Collaborate with project teams to ensure product development processes meet regulatory requirements and support business needs
  • Provide guidance to project teams on regulatory strategy and requirements, with support from RA leadership as needed
  • Support regulatory deliverables on behalf of internal and external program teams
  • Provide summaries and regulatory education within project subteams and in support of project planning

Process Improvement, Metrics, and Mentoring

  • Prepare metrics for regulatory management reporting and help identify areas for improvement
  • Contribute to and help lead process improvements that enhance the effectiveness of the regulatory affairs department
  • Support RA leadership in implementing data-driven improvements in RA processes and department initiatives
  • Provide onboarding support, guidance, and informal training to junior RA staff and project teams
  • Contribute to setting individual and departmental annual goals aligned with business objectives
  • Take on special projects that support department goals

Professional Development

  • Build specialized knowledge of regulatory guidelines and requirements in one or more fields applicable to Natera
  • Develop cross-functional leadership skills and core competencies in regulatory affairs
  • Perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in biology, chemistry, engineering, or a related field
  • 7-10 years of work experience in the medical device, in vitro diagnostic, or pharmaceutical industry, or a relevant combination of skills, education, and experience
  • Direct regulatory affairs experience, preferably with 510(k)s, INDs, IDEs, PMAs, or BLAs

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Proficiency with computer applications (MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.)
  • Good technical writing and communication skills
  • Independent worker and self-starter with strong organizational and planning skills
  • Ability to be productive and successful in an intense work environment
  • Good judgment and excellent attention to detail
  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal skills, with the flexibility to collaborate on multiple projects

Physical Demands and Work Environment

  • Approximately 10% travel, with flexibility required to meet changing business needs
  • Duties are typically performed in an office setting and require the ability to use a computer keyboard, communicate over the telephone, and read printed material
  • Duties may occasionally require working outside normal hours (evenings and weekends)

The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. This may differ in other locations due to cost of labor considerations.
Remote USA
$83,000—$103,700 USD

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.

WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program!

For more information, visit www.natera.com.

Natera is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace environment, and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. Inclusive collaboration benefits our employees, our community and our patients, and is critical to our mission of changing the management of disease worldwide.

All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply, and will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, age, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with applicable laws.

If you are based in California, we encourage you to read this important information for California residents. 

Link: https://www.natera.com/notice-of-data-collection-california-residents/

Email communications from all other domain names are not from Natera or its employees and are fraudulent. Natera does not request interviews via text messages and does not ask for personal information until a candidate has engaged with the company and has spoken to a recruiter and the hiring team.
